scenes.text: How to evaluate a casino game aggregator, before you sign. Seven questions you can answer yourself, without a single sales call.

Most operators comparing aggregators are not unhappy. A contract is up for renewal, or a new market changes the content you need. Start with the question that decides everything else: are you buying a content layer, or a whole platform? Comparing one against the other, without saying so, is how procurement goes wrong.

One. Catalog fit, not catalog size. Whether the game providers your market plays are licensed in your jurisdictions matters more than any headline number on a homepage. Two. The integration model. Be explicit about what you are buying. Three. Documentation you can read today. Vague docs before a contract rarely improve after one.

Four. Wallet semantics. Ask exactly how duplicate transaction I Ds, rollbacks, timeouts and disconnected rounds are handled. This is where integrations hurt, months later. Five. Reporting granularity. Per-game, per-provider and per-player, close to real time, with exports your B I stack can read.

Six. Commercial flexibility. Contract length, minimums, revenue share, and what happens if a market closes. Flexibility at signature is easier to get than at renewal. Seven. Exit cost. The more of your stack sits with one vendor, the harder a future migration becomes.

Whichever names end up on your shortlist, judge them all the same way. We would rather you tested the shortlist than took our word for it. Book a walkthrough with our team at iplaygames dot A I. iPlay Games.
